annotation_description: DSV3 Analyst chose to take Beast Within with Thoughtseize from Qwen3L Dreamer's hand. While Beast Within is a versatile instant-speed removal spell that could threaten DSV3's permanents (including key enchantments like Pernicious Deed or Sylvan Library), Rishkar's Expertise is arguably the highest-impact card in the hand. Rishkar's Expertise can generate massive card advantage by drawing cards equal to greatest power AND casting a free spell with MV 5 or less. In a multiplayer game, denying that kind of card advantage engine is typically more impactful than removing a reactive removal spell. Rishkar, Peema Renegade is also notable as it enables mana ramp and enables Rishkar's Expertise to draw more cards. However, Beast Within is the card most likely to directly disrupt DSV3's game plan (destroying Pernicious Deed, Sylvan Library, or key lands), so there's a reasonable argument for taking it.

message: Choose spell or ability to play: Sensei's Divining Top
chosen_display: 1. {1}: Look at the top three cards of your library, then put them back in any order.
annotation_description: Put Darkblast on top of library instead of Overgrown Tomb, meaning they'll draw Darkblast and potentially miss their 4th land drop. With Pernicious Deed (1BG) and Mystical Teachings (3U) in hand, hitting the 4th land is important for casting these key spells on curve. Darkblast is narrow and doesn't address any immediate threat.

Qwen3L Dreamer put a +1/+1 counter on an opponent's creature (Hada Spy Patrol, controlled by MiniMx Spike) instead of putting both counters on their own creatures. Rishkar's ability lets you put counters on up to two target creatures — they already targeted their own Rishkar, but the second counter went to an opponent's Hada Spy Patrol. This gives MiniMx Spike a free +1/+1 counter (making the Spy Patrol a 2/2 unblockable creature or advancing its level-up), and also gives it the ability to tap for {G} due to Rishkar's second ability. There's no benefit to buffing an opponent's creature here, especially an evasive one.

Casting Kaima before playing the Mountain from hand. The land drop should come first to maximize available mana (leaving extra mana open after casting Kaima) and to increase Blackblade Reforged's bonus by 1. Playing lands before spells is fundamental sequencing.

The 2/2 Knight Token with vigilance could attack for free since vigilance means it stays untapped for blocking. Against DSV3 Analyst who has no creatures, both could attack safely for 3 total damage instead of just 1.

message: Select 2 cards of cards drawn this turn (selected 0 of 2, min 2)
annotation_description: With Sylvan Library, DSV3 Analyst drew three lands (Island, Overgrown Tomb, Windswept Heath). They need to select 2 to either pay 4 life each or put back on top of library. Selecting Island as one of the two to put back/pay life for is reasonable since it's the weakest card. However, the key question is what the second card should be and whether to pay life. The decision is still in progress (only selected 1 of 2 so far), but choosing Island first is fine. The real consideration is that keeping Windswept Heath (a fetchland) is generally better than keeping a basic Island since it provides deck thinning and can fetch Overgrown Tomb later. Putting Island back on top of the library is the right call for one of the two returns.

Tapping/untapping Propaganda with Derevi's trigger accomplishes nothing. Enchantments' static abilities function regardless of tapped/untapped status - Propaganda still forces opponents to pay {2} per attacking creature whether it's tapped or not.

message: Choose spell or ability to play: Miscalculation
chosen_display: 1. Cast Miscalculation: Counter target spell unless its controller pays {2}.
annotation_description: Using Miscalculation (a soft counter) on Doomed Necromancer, a modest 2/2 creature that needs to survive a turn to activate. The opponent can simply pay {2} to resolve it anyway. DSV3 has Darkblast in hand which cleanly kills the 2/2 Necromancer, and Pernicious Deed in hand as a sweeper option. In a 4-player game, saving counterspells for more impactful threats is generally better.

DSV3 Analyst missed their land drop entirely this turn despite having 3 lands in hand (Overgrown Tomb, Windswept Heath, Island) and only 3 lands on battlefield. At 13 life with key cards like Pernicious Deed and Baleful Strix waiting to be cast, developing mana was critical. The turn ended with no land played and no spells cast.

DSV3 Analyst is at 12 life with zero creatures to block. Qwen3L Dreamer has Rishkar (~3/3), Kaima (3/3), and Whiptongue Hydra (4/4+) available to attack, representing 10+ damage to an undefended player. Skipping attacks entirely wastes a massive damage opportunity against a vulnerable opponent. Propaganda only taxes attacks against Sonnet Story, not DSV3 Analyst.

Qwen3L Dreamer cast Rishkar's Expertise during the combat phase (the message says 'Play spells and abilities' during COMBAT). Rishkar's Expertise is a sorcery and cannot be cast during combat. However, looking more carefully at the game state, the reasoning mentions 'postcombat main phase' but the decision header says 'Turn 8 COMBAT'. More importantly, the reasoning is completely incoherent - it discusses equipping Blackblade Reforged and Whiptongue Hydra (which isn't on the battlefield), then trails off, yet the actual choice was Rishkar's Expertise. With only 6 mana available (3 Mountains, 2 Forests, 1 Exotic Orchard = 6 lands, but some may be tapped), casting Rishkar's Expertise costs 4GG. The greatest power among their creatures appears to be Kaima at 3/3, so they'd draw 3 cards and get a free spell of MV 5 or less. This is actually a reasonable play if they have the mana. However, they also have Rampant Rejuvenator in hand and an unplayed Mountain. They should play the Mountain first before casting Rishkar's Expertise to have more mana available afterward and to boost Blackblade Reforged's potential. Playing the land before the sorcery is strictly better sequencing.

At 7 life with Sensei's Divining Top available, DSV3 Analyst passed on activating it before making main phase decisions. Activating Top for {1} to see the top 3 cards would provide valuable information to guide the rest of the turn (e.g., whether to play Watery Grave untapped, which land to play, whether to cast Brainstorm now or later).

The reasoning references destroying a '13/13 Hydra' that doesn't appear to be on the battlefield based on the board state shown. If Putrefy is being cast on a less critical target when Pernicious Deed (a powerful board wipe) and Baleful Strix (cantrip + deathtouch blocker) are available and DSV3 Analyst is at a critical 5 life, casting Pernicious Deed for future insurance and Baleful Strix for an immediate blocker may be more valuable.

At 5 life, DSV3 Analyst cast Putrefy (likely targeting Kaima) but the reasoning references targeting 'the Hydra' which isn't on the battlefield, suggesting confused threat assessment. More importantly, they should have played a land first (Windswept Heath or Wooded Foothills from hand) before casting spells - basic sequencing. Additionally, deploying Pernicious Deed as a deterrent board wipe threat would provide better protection at 5 life than a single targeted removal, since Deed discourages all opponents from overcommitting.

At 5 life, DSV3 Analyst tapped Cephalid Coliseum (which deals 1 damage to its controller) to pay the generic mana cost of Putrefy, unnecessarily losing 1 life to go to 4. They had multiple painless alternatives: Overgrown Tomb could produce {B}, Underground Sea could produce {B}, and Watery Grave could produce {B}, any combination of which could cover {1}{B}{G} without using Cephalid Coliseum.

message: Select up to one an artifact, a creature, or a land
annotation_description: Sacrificed Rishkar, Peema Renegade to Sandfall Cell instead of a duplicate basic land. Rishkar provides mana acceleration (creatures with counters tap for G) and is a body, while sacrificing one of the duplicate Mountains or Forests would have minimal impact with 5 lands on board.

message: Select a player, planeswalker, or battle to attack
annotation_description: MiniMx Spike had to discard down to 7 cards at end of turn, suggesting they didn't use all their mana this turn. They could have added a storage counter to Saltcrusted Steppe during combat for free future value, since the mana ended up going unused.

Sword of the Paruns is a slow equipment that requires significant additional mana investment (3 to equip, 3 to activate) and MiniMx Spike only has one creature (Hada Spy Patrol). Meanwhile, Acidic Slime is castable and would destroy Propaganda, which is actively taxing MiniMx Spike's attacks against Sonnet Story. Removing Propaganda while adding a 2/2 deathtouch body is far more impactful.

message: Choose spell or ability to play: Sword of the Paruns
chosen_display: 1. {3}: You may tap or untap equipped creature.
annotation_description: Activating Sword of the Paruns to tap/untap the equipped creature during precombat main with no clear strategic purpose. With only Hada Spy Patrol on the battlefield and 8 lands available, this wastes 3 mana that could be used toward casting Darksteel Ingot (3 mana ramp/fixing) or Swiftfoot Boots (2 mana) to develop the board.

In a 1v1 against Sonnet Story with Propaganda up, MiniMx Spike spent mana leveling up Hada Spy Patrol (which already had hexproof from Swiftfoot Boots and was unblockable at level 1-2) instead of deploying Skyward Eye Prophets, a powerful card advantage engine that would help close out the game. The shroud from level 3 is largely redundant with hexproof from boots.
